title: Courtland Avenue East mid-rise and Sportsworld towers
subtitle: Committee backed a six-storey rental-or-condo building and deferred a 30-storey tower proposal amid traffic, parkland and school bus concerns.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee held two public hearings under the Planning Act. It recommended approval of Official Plan and zoning changes for a six-storey apartment building at 45-53 Courtland Avenue East, with minor amendments proposed by staff on the day {{vote:m1}}. The changes clarify that density is measured by floor space ratio and that parking is set only as rates. Residents of the neighbouring area spoke in support, citing the developer's changes to the design after consultation.

The committee also considered a much larger proposal for 4396 King Street East and 25 Sportsworld Drive, with two towers of 30 and 18 storeys and an eight-storey building. Delegates opposed it, mainly over traffic, parkland and school bus safety. The committee recommended deferring the decision to the March 20, 2023 Council meeting so staff can gather more information {{vote:m2}}.

For residents, the first item moves toward Council with a site walk planned for neighbours. The second means the King Street and Sportsworld proposal will not be decided until Council has further information on traffic, highway access, amenity space and sustainable energy options.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the Official Plan amendment and approving the zoning change for the Cantiro Courtland GP project, as amended by staff, with no further public notice required.

decisions.item: Sportsworld Shopping Centre and Taylorwood Park Homes
decisions.detail: The committee recommended deferring the Official Plan and zoning applications for 4396 King Street East and 25 Sportsworld Drive to the March 20, 2023 Council meeting for further review of traffic, MTO connections, school bus loading, amenity space and sustainable energy options.

debate: On Courtland Avenue, a neighbourhood delegate supported the change despite reservations about the increased floor space ratio. The delegate pointed to a rear setback of more than 19 metres, regrading of the site, and design changes made after feedback, and asked for a site walk on fencing, lighting and grading.

Councillors asked about parking at the Courtland site, where parking is set at a rate below one space per unit. Staff said the location near transit and downtown, plus bicycle parking, made spillover onto streets unlikely. Councillors also asked why no affordable units were proposed. The applicant's planner said the developer had instead increased the affordable share at its King Street project.

Delegates opposing the Sportsworld proposal said the traffic study already described the intersection as strained, there was too little greenspace, parking was inadequate, excavation could affect well water, and school buses had nowhere to stop. Some said their concerns had been ignored.

Staff said the Region, the Ministry of Transportation and City transportation staff accepted the traffic study, which found marginal impacts. They said school bus loading, geothermal and final amenity space would be settled at site plan stage. Several councillors still questioned how current the 2021 traffic study was and how it treated congestion and the future LRT.

Councillors raised the height of a 30-storey tower in an area with no existing skyline, climate and heating concerns, and the lack of nearby parks. Staff noted that holding provisions could tie the second phase to LRT timing, though that was not recommended.
